grades.quote: A `FENCE` (with _fm_ = `0000` ) orders all memory operations in its predecessor set before all memory operations in its successor set.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary background on data-memory fencing, but does not explain FENCE.I or instruction-fetch synchronization.

grades.quote: RISC-V does not guarantee that stores to instruction memory will be made visible to instruction fetches on a RISC-V hart until that hart executes a FENCE.I instruction. A FENCE.I instruction ensures that a subsequent instruction fetch on a RISC-V hart will see any previous data stores already visible to the same RISC-V hart. FENCE.I does _not_ ensure that other RISC-V harts' instruction fetches will observe the local hart’s stores in a multiprocessor system. To make a store to instruction memory visible to all RISC-V harts, the writing hart also has to execute a data FENCE before requesting that all remote RISC-V harts execute a FENCE.I.
grades.reason: Directly explains the required synchronization before fetching modified instructions, including local and remote harts.
Discusses reserved FENCE fields and memory-model rationale, not when FENCE.I is needed for modified code.
